what_it_does: Cuzco is a high-performance processor design that follows the RISC-V instruction set architecture (RISC-V is a free, open standard for CPU design—like x86 or ARM, but vendor-neutral). The paper presents a complete, production-ready implementation of Cuzco that combines pipelined execution (where multiple instructions run simultaneously, each in different stages) with out-of-order instruction scheduling (allowing the processor to reorder operations for speed if later instructions don't depend on earlier ones). It includes optimized memory caches designed for fast access. The design is fully compatible with RVA23 (a profile specifying which RISC-V features are included), making it suitable for both data center and edge device deployment.
